Sam Rivera: :rotating_light: Urgent — new CVE affecting libcrypto/OpenSSL 3.x surfaced in vendor advisory. Looks like both ubuntu:22.04 base images (glibc-linked) and alpine:3.18 (musl) need a coordinated rollforward. Need quick triage: rebuild vs patch backport, KMS image signing, and RBAC for signer roles.
Maya Chen: On it. Can you drop the advisory link?
Sam Rivera: https://example.vendor/cve-2026-XXXX — summary: crafted input may trigger crash or predictable state. Vendor released 3.0.10 and backports for stable.
Jordan Patel: For ubuntu images, glibc overlay may require a full rebuild to ensure correct linking. For alpine, we can rebuild smaller layers but need to verify musl compat with the new libssl symbols.
Alex Kim: Risk matrix: if we do a quick rebuild with upgraded openssl package, we must run canary on prod-facing runtime images (inference runtime) and on CI images that run fuzz tests. How long to get canaries out?
Maya Chen: I can schedule a canary slice tonight. Suggest 5% traffic, 2h soak, and regression tests: perf, kv-cache sanity, and TLS handshake fuzz.
Sam Rivera: Also: signing. We must sign rebuilt artifacts with our KMS key and publish attestations. Question: do we need to rotate signer RBAC to a dedicated ops service account to limit blast radius?
security-ops: Yes — prefer dedicated signer role with least privilege. We'll create a short-lived signing principal for the rebuild job and record all actions in audit logs.
Jordan Patel: CI changes: add post-build attestation step: 
```
# pseudo
docker build -t redwood/runtime:openssl-3.0.10 .
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/rw/keys/signer-001 redwood/runtime:openssl-3.0.10
attestctl create --artifact redwood/runtime:openssl-3.0.10 --suite fuzz-results-2026-03-20
```
Sam Rivera: Nice. Two questions: 1) cosign with KMS URL — do we have RBAC for the deploy pipeline? 2) audit log retention for attestations — security needs 365d.
security-ops: 1) We'll add the pipeline SA to the signer binding for this key. We'll scope to a single key and limit to Put/Sign operations. 2) Audit logs will be forwarded to the central SIEM; retention policy already covers 1 year. We'll make an explicit entry in the rebuild runbook.
Alex Kim: Regression risk: we saw an earlier rebuild that caused a quantization regression on arm64 due to different math lib linking. Can we run a small perf matrix: x86_64/gpu, arm64/cpu, arm64/gpu?
Maya Chen: I'll add perf matrix to canary plan. Also adding a smoke test for model outputs (determinism check for a few prompts).
Jordan Patel: Patch vs full rebuild tradeoff: backporting openssl only (installing vendor package) reduces rebuild scope but may leave other libs out-of-sync. Given glibc interaction on ubuntu, prefer full baseimage rebuild for ubuntu targets and package upgrade for alpine slim images where feasible.
Sam Rivera: Agreed. Proposed rollout: 
- Stage 1 (today): Rebuild alpine:3.18 minimal runtime images with openssl 3.0.10, sign, attest, run canary (5%) for 2h.
- Stage 2 (tomorrow morning): Full ubuntu:22.04 baseimage rebuild, run CI matrix and extended canary (10%) for 6h.
- Stage 3: Promote to prod and rotate keys if any compromise indicators found.
Maya Chen: Timeline okay. Assigning owners: alpine rebuild => Maya. ubuntu rebuild => Jordan. Signing + IAM => security-ops. Runbook updates => Alex.
Sam Rivera: Owner ack? @Maya Chen @Jordan Patel @security-ops @Alex Kim
Maya Chen: ack ✅
Jordan Patel: ack ✅ I'll start the ubuntu pipeline prep now. Expect PR by EOD with Dockerfile bump and package pins.
security-ops: Starting signer policy change ticket and will provision a temporary principal for the pipeline. Ticket: SEC-2026-125.
Alex Kim: I'll add the canary dashboard (latency, errors, model-diff rate) and hook up alerts to eng-oncall. Also will add a CI gate to abort promotion if fuzz regressions > 0.
Sam Rivera: Nice. One gotcha: some downstream vendor libs in our multi-stage builds pull old openssl versions in buildkit cache. Add `--no-cache` for critical layers and rebuild base layer images first.
Jordan Patel: Good catch. We'll also run SBOM diff to ensure no older openssl remains: `syft packages redwood/runtime:tag -o json | jq '.[] | select(.name=="openssl")'`
Maya Chen: I ran local smoke with musl and saw one test flake on arm64 linking. I'll log it in the PR and mark it non-blocking for alpine canary, but will block ubuntu promotion until resolved.
Sam Rivera: Action items summary (short):
- Maya: alpine rebuild + canary tonight, no-cache, cosign + attest.
- Jordan: ubuntu full rebuild + CI matrix, SBOM diff.
- security-ops: signer RBAC ticket, temp principal, ensure audit forwarding.
- Alex: canary dashboards + CI gates.
- Sam: coordinate rollout and update incident channel if any regression.
security-ops: Noted. We'll also enable KMS access logging for the signer key to have an additional trail.
Sam Rivera: Cool. If anyone hits a blocker ping me in #incidents and DM. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Build pipeline started for PR #4321 (ubuntu-rebuild-openssl) — status: queued.
Maya Chen: CI queued for alpine PR #4320 — I'll monitor and post results here.
Jordan Patel: PR #4321 up: dockerfile bump, package list, SBOM attached. Link: https://git.example/rw/runtime/pulls/4321
Maya Chen: Alpine build succeeded. Cosign signing successful. Attestation entry: attest-2026-2099990000. Canary warmed to 5% now.
Sam Rivera: Great. Keep notes in the runbook and mark the rollback playbook section updated.
Alex Kim: Canary metrics look clean at 90m. No perf or model-diff anomalies so far.
Maya Chen: Holding on arm64 flake logs, will triage tomorrow.
Sam Rivera: OK closing this thread for now — follow-ups in the PRs and SEC ticket. Thanks everyone.
